What is the reference period or as-of date on the percentage of women age 65 and older who had a dental visit in the past 12 months in 2022?
response_text:
**Reference period: calendar year 2022** — specifically, NHIS data collected January–December 2022.

Two distinct time elements are stacked in that 64.9% figure:

- **Data-collection period (the "as-of"):** 2022. The estimate is an annual, single-year estimate from the National Health Interview Survey, with interviews spread across the whole calendar year.
- **Recall/exposure window:** the 12 months preceding each respondent's interview. It's a rolling lookback, not a fixed window — a woman interviewed in February 2022 is reporting on roughly March 2021–February 2022, while one interviewed in November 2022 covers December 2021–November 2022.

So the correct as-of statement is "2022," and the correct full characterization is: *among women age 65 and older, 64.9% (95% CI 63.1–66.6) had a dental visit in the 12 months preceding interview, United States, 2022.* There is no single calendar interval covered by all respondents, which is why NCHS labels it by survey year rather than by date range.

One caveat worth stating: the excerpt you pasted doesn't include the source line or data-note section, so the survey name is inferred from the structure (percent, 95% CI, standard error, 65+ by sex/age/race-Hispanic origin, 2022) — that pattern is NCHS/NHIS. If you have the full brief, the "Data source and methods" section will confirm the survey and state the collection period explicitly.
